# Summary

## Project Context
BlackrockMU private server client at `F:\blackrockmu`. User (Portuguese speaker) owns/administers the server but has **no access to it** (it's at `145.239.149.84`, a remote machine). The project has two main parts: the `byp.dll` bypass (C++, injected into the game via `opengl32.dll` proxy) and `MuProxy2` (C# WinForms control UI).

## Task 1: HWID multibox fix (COMPLETED & VERIFIED)
The server rejected the 2nd game instance with `F1 01 07` (anti-multibox, one session per HWID). User chose client-side fix (byp rewrites HWID per instance) over server-side (no access).

**Implementation** (`byp/gg_bypass2/`):
- New `src/packets/HwidRewrite.cpp` + `src/include/HwidRewrite.h` — intercepts the login packet (`C1 5F F1` inside SM-encrypted `C3`, inside Layer-1), finds the 35-char HWID (`XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX`), replaces it per-instance, re-encrypts (XorData → SM → Layer-1), with fail-safe (any error → send original).
- Derivation: base 0 → real HWID; base >0 → last DWORD XOR `base * 2654435761`. Override via `MUPROXY_HWID` env var.
- Wired into `HookSend` (`WinsockHooks.cpp`) and `dllmain.cpp`; added to `build.bat`.
- Verified via Python simulation (SM round-trip with real keys from logs, full pipeline) — all passed. User confirmed "funcionou".

**Key technical facts**: HWID is 35 chars (not 36). Login packet: Layer-1 (XOR 0x36/sub 0x07) → C3 (SimpleModulus) → C1 F1 → XorData payload. HWID at offset ~59. SM keys from log: Mod=[0001F44F 00028386 0001125B 0001A192], Enc=[00005BC1 00002E87 00004D68 0000354F], Dec=[00007B38 000007FF 0000DEB3 000027C7], Xor=[0000BD1D 0000B455 00003B43 00009239].

## Task 2: MuProxy2 UI redesign (IN PROGRESS — designer fix just deployed)
User wanted the UI modernized ("anti-gamer", ugly, broken layout). I rewrote the UI with a dark modern theme. Multiple iterations:

**Files created/modified** (`byp/MuProxy2/MuProxy2/`):
- `Theme.cs` (new) — modern palette (Bg `#0F1115`, Surface `#181B22`, Accent `#E3B341`, Text `#E8E9EB`, TextMuted `#B2B8C4`), Segoe UI fonts, `EnableDarkTitleBar` (DWM), `Apply()` that styles all controls at runtime.
- `Controls.cs` (new) — `DarkTabControl` (dark tab strip, owner-draw) and `ModernGroupBox` (rounded border, amber title, replaces white-bordered GroupBox).
- `MainForm.Designer.cs` — fully rewritten: header (logo + "BLACKROCK MU · DIRECT HOOK"), 4 tabs (General/Custom Stuff/Packets/Logs), banner panel, status strip, all controls repositioned.
- `MainForm.cs` — `SetupLogFilters` uses dark theme + `logsTop` panel; added `OnLoad` override calling `Theme.Apply(this)`; `lblPotionState` color fix.

**Critical fix (designer was broken)**: User reported the VS designer showed no components and black-on-black text. Root cause: I had put `Theme.Apply(this)` and dark colors inside `InitializeComponent` (which the designer parses/executes). **Fix**: removed ALL `Theme.*` references from `InitializeComponent` (designer now shows a default white form, fully editable); theme is applied only at runtime in `OnLoad`.

**Crash fix**: App crashed with `ArgumentException: Parameter is not valid` in `ModernGroupBox.OnPaint` (`MeasureString`). Fixed by using a fresh `new Font("Segoe UI", ...)` + `TextRenderer.MeasureText` + try/catch. Also replaced all `"Segoe UI Semibold"` → `"Segoe UI"` (font family issue).

**Status**: Build succeeds (0 errors), app launches without crashing, deployed to `bin\Debug\net8.0-windows\MuProxy2.exe`. **The designer fix is UNVERIFIED** — I cannot test the VS designer directly; user must confirm. The user's two game instances (base 0/100) were closed by the user; they need to relaunch to get the new build.

## Task 3: In-game imgui menu (DEFERRED)
User asked if attack config/skill/auto-potion could appear in-game via imgui. I investigated: game uses OpenGL fixed-function (no shaders in proxy exports), byp has no render/input hooks yet. User then said "ok vamos deixar isso querto" (let's leave that aside) and redirected to the designer fix.
